definitions.explanation: A widespread infectious disease that affects many people in a region at the same time. Used broadly for both historical plagues and modern epidemics, often with a somewhat literary or formal tone.

examples.japanese: {疫病|えきびょう}が{広|ひろ}がった。
{中世|ちゅうせい}ヨーロッパでは{疫病|えきびょう}で{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{亡|な}くなった。
examples.english: In medieval Europe, many people died from epidemics.

examples.japanese: {疫病|えきびょう}の{流行|りゅうこう}を{防|ふせ}ぐために、{政府|せいふ}は{厳|きび}しい{対策|たいさく}を{取|と}った。
examples.english: In order to prevent the spread of the epidemic, the government took strict measures.

notes:
USAGE:
A somewhat formal or literary word for epidemic or plague. In modern Japanese, {感染症|かんせんしょう} (infectious disease) and {伝染病|でんせんびょう} (contagious disease) are more common in everyday and medical contexts, while {疫病|えきびょう} tends to appear in historical narratives and dramatic descriptions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {疫病|えきびょう}が{流行|りゅうこう}する: an epidemic breaks out
- {疫病|えきびょう}が{蔓延|まんえん}する: an epidemic spreads widely
- {疫病|えきびょう}に{罹|かか}る: to contract an epidemic disease
- {疫病神|やくびょうがみ}: god of pestilence; jinx, person who brings bad luck
